grammar.title: Basic word order
grammar.rule: Subject + Verb + Object. Time and place come before the verb.
body: Chinese verbs never change form: no tense endings, no -s. Who does it, when and where it happens come from the surrounding words.
There are no articles (a, the). Nouns have no plural form. A modifier always comes before what it describes, and time words sit before the verb, not at the end.
Short answers and greetings can be complete sentences without a subject or verb (你好！ 谢谢！). These are the 'non-subject-predicate' sentences in the syllabus.
tips: English puts 'tomorrow' at the end. Chinese puts it before the verb: 我 明天 去, not 我 去 明天.

ex.en: I am going to school tomorrow.

grammar.title: 是: A is B
grammar.rule: A 是 B links two nouns. Negative: A 不 是 B.
body: 是 joins nouns and pronouns: identity, category, description. It is not used before an adjective (use 很 instead, see the adjective lesson).
Question: add 吗, or use the A-not-A form 是不是.
tips: Wrong: 我 是 很 忙. Right: 我 很 忙.

grammar.title: Adjectives as predicates
grammar.rule: Subject + 很 + Adjective. No 是.
body: An adjective can be the predicate by itself, with no 'to be'. In a plain statement it normally takes 很, which here is a weak linking word and does not always mean 'very'.
Without any degree word the sentence sounds like a comparison. For the negative use 不 and drop 很.
tips: To really mean 'very', stress it: 非常 or 真. Plain 很 is just the linking word.

grammar.title: Yes/no questions with 吗
grammar.rule: Statement + 吗 ？
body: Put 吗 at the end of a statement. The word order does not change.
Answer by repeating the verb: 是 / 不 是, 有 / 没有, 喜欢 / 不 喜欢.
tips: Never combine 吗 with a question word: 你 叫 什么 名字 吗 is wrong.

grammar.title: Question words
grammar.cn: 特指问句 / 疑问代词
grammar.rule: Replace the unknown part with the question word. The word order stays the same as the answer.
body: 什么 what, 谁 who, 哪儿 / 哪里 where, 几 how many (small numbers), 多少 how many / how much, 怎么 how, 哪 which.
几 expects a number under about ten and is followed by a measure word (几 口 人). 多少 works for any quantity and the measure word is optional.
patterns: 你 叫 什么 名字 ？
tips: Answer 你 去 哪儿 ？ with 我 去 学校, not with 在 哪儿.

ex.en: How many people are in your family?
How do you get to school?

grammar.title: Choice and A-not-A questions
grammar.cn: 选择问句 / 正反问句
grammar.rule: A 还是 B ？ offers a choice. V 不 V ？ asks yes or no.
body: 还是 means 'or' in questions. Repeat the verb if you like: 喝 茶 还是 喝 水.
The A-not-A form puts the positive and negative side by side: 去 不 去, 好 不 好, 是不是. It replaces 吗.
tips: 还是 is for questions. In statements 'or' is a different word (not needed at HSK 1).

ex.en: Do you want tea or water?

grammar.title: 有 and 没有
grammar.rule: 有 = to have, and also 'there is'. Negative: 没有. Never 不有.
body: Possession: 我 有 一 个 哥哥. Existence: place + 有 + thing.
Questions: 你 有 手机 吗 ？ or 你 有 没有 手机 ？
tips: The thing that exists comes last: 桌子 上边 有 书, not 有 书 在 桌子 上边.

ex.en: I don't have an older sister.
There is a book on the table.
There are a bed and a table in the room.

grammar.title: 不 and 没
grammar.cn: 否定副词: 不 / 没(有) / 别
grammar.rule: 不 for habits, wishes and facts. 没(有) for 'did not' and 'does not have'.
body: 不 negates ordinary verbs, adjectives, and the future or a decision: 我 不 吃 肉, 明天 我 不 去.
没 or 没有 negates what did not happen, and the verb 有: 他 没 去 学校 (he did not go), 我 没有 钱.
Tone change: 不 is read bú before a 4th-tone syllable, so 不 是 sounds like bú shì and 不 去 like bú qù.
tips: After 没 the completion 了 is normally dropped: 我 没 吃饭, not 我 没 吃饭 了.

ex.en: He did not go to school today.

grammar.title: Numbers
grammar.rule: 一 二 三 四 五 六 七 八 九 十. Build bigger numbers by stacking.
body: 十一 is 十 一, twenty is 二 十, twenty-one is 二 十 一. One hundred is 一 百. Zero is 零 (or 〇).
Use 两 instead of 二 before a measure word: 两 个 人, 两 杯 茶. Use 二 when counting, in phone numbers, and in 第二.
一 changes tone: yí before a 4th tone (一 个 yí gè), yì before 1st, 2nd and 3rd tones. It stays yī when counting alone.
tips: Wrong: 二 个 人. Right: 两 个 人.

ex.en: There are three people in my family.

grammar.title: Measure words
grammar.rule: Number + Measure word + Noun. 这 / 那 / 几 also need one.
body: 个 is the all-purpose measure word. Others at this level: 口 for family members, 本 for books, 杯 for cups of drink, 块 for yuan and pieces, 家 for shops and restaurants, 间 for rooms, 页 for pages.
A number plus a measure word forms a 'number-measure phrase', which can modify a noun or answer how many.
patterns: 这 / 那 / 几 + Measure + Noun
tips: When unsure, 个 is usually understood. Learn 口 for family and 本 for books first.

ex.en: I would like two cups of tea.
There are four people in my family.

grammar.title: Pronouns and 们
grammar.rule: 我 你 您 他 她 + 们 for plural.
body: 我们 we, 你们 you (plural), 他们 / 她们 they. 您 is the polite singular 'you'. 们 can also follow a noun for people: 朋友们.
他 and 她 sound the same (tā). 别人 means 'other people'.
patterns: 我 / 你 / 他 / 她 + 们
tips: Do not use 们 after a number: 三 个 朋友, not 三 个 朋友们.

grammar.title: 的 for possession and description
grammar.rule: A 的 B: A belongs to or describes B.
body: Possession: 我 的 书. Description: adjective + 的 + noun, 好看 的 衣服.
With close relations and places you can drop 的: 我 妈妈, 我 家, 我们 学校.
To say 'mine' put 的 last: 是 我 的 。
tips: A single-syllable adjective usually goes straight before the noun: 大 房子, 新 手机.

grammar.title: This, that and where
grammar.rule: 这 / 那 + (Measure) + Noun. 这儿 / 那儿 / 哪儿 for places.
body: 这 this, 那 that. Plurals: 这些, 那些, 哪些. Places: 这儿 / 这里 here, 那儿 / 那里 there, 哪儿 / 哪里 where.
Before a noun add a measure word: 这 本 书, 那 个 人.
tips: 这儿 and 那儿 are the everyday forms; 这里 and 那里 are slightly more formal.

ex.en: There is a shop over there.

grammar.title: Telling the time and date
grammar.rule: Big to small: year, month, day, weekday, hour. Time words go before the verb.
body: Dates: 月 month and 号 day (spoken), 日 in writing: 十 月 十 六 号. Weekdays: 星期 + number: 星期 一 … 星期 六, and 星期天 / 星期日 for Sunday.
Clock: 三 点 three o'clock, 三 点 半 half past, 三 点 十 五 分 3:15. Ask: 现在 几 点 ？ 今天 星期 几 ？ 今天 几 月 几 号 ？
tips: Say 两 点 (two o'clock), not 二 点.

ex.en: I get up at seven in the morning.
What time do you start work?

grammar.title: 在 for location
grammar.rule: A 在 place = A is at place. 在 place + verb = does it at place.
body: As a verb: 他 在 家. As a preposition: 我 在 学校 学习 汉语. The place phrase comes before the action verb.
Negative: 不 在.
tips: Wrong: 我 学习 汉语 在 学校. The place comes before the verb.

grammar.title: Doing right now
grammar.cn: 进行态: 在 / 正在 / 呢
grammar.rule: (正) 在 + Verb (+ 呢) shows an action in progress.
body: 在 or 正在 before a verb means the action is happening now. 呢 can close the sentence for a lively feel, and 呢 alone can also carry this meaning.
Negative: 没 在 + verb.
tips: This 在 is placed directly before the verb. The place version of 在 has a place word right after it.

grammar.title: 了 after a verb: finished
grammar.cn: 动态助词 “了1” / 完成态
grammar.rule: Verb + 了 shows the action is completed.
body: Put 了 right after the verb. If there is an object it usually carries a number or description: 吃 了 两 个 包子.
Negative: 没 (有) + verb, and 了 disappears.
tips: 了 marks completion, not the past. Habitual past actions don't take it.

ex.en: I didn't go to school yesterday.

grammar.title: 了 at the end: new situation
grammar.cn: 语气助词 “了2” / 变化态
grammar.rule: … 了 says things have changed or a new situation has begun.
body: Sentence-final 了 signals a change: it has started raining, I became hungry, it is now three o'clock.
It also appears in 太 … 了, the exclamation 'too …!'.
tips: Both 了 can appear together: 我 吃 了 饭 了 means I've eaten (and the situation has changed).

grammar.title: 想, 要, 会, 能
grammar.rule: Modal + Verb: 想 would like to, 要 want or need, 会 know how or will, 能 can or be able.
body: 想 expresses a wish: 我 想 去 北京. 要 is a stronger want, or 'going to': 我 要 一 杯 茶.
会 is learned skill or likelihood: 他 会 说 汉语, 明天 会 下雨. 能 is ability or circumstance: 你 能 来 吗 ？
Negatives: 不 想, 不 会, 不 能. 'Don't want to' is 不 想, while a command 'don't' is 别.
patterns: Subject + 想 / 要 / 会 / 能 + Verb
tips: Use 会 for 'can' when it is learned, 能 when it is possible right now.

ex.en: I want to go to Beijing.
I would like a cup of tea.

grammar.title: 也, 都, 还, 先, 再
grammar.rule: Adverbs come after the subject and before the verb.
body: 也 also, 都 all, 还 still / also, 先 first, 再 then / again (later), 就 right away, 马上 immediately, 常常 often.
When 也 and 都 meet, 也 comes first: 我们 也 都 是 学生. They never go at the end of the sentence.
patterns: Subject + 也 / 都 / 还 / 先 / 再 + Verb
tips: Wrong: 我 去 也. Right: 我 也 去.

ex.en: I want to eat first, then go to school.
He often goes to bed late.

grammar.title: 很, 太, 非常, 真, 最
grammar.rule: Degree word + Adjective.
body: 很 very, 非常 extremely, 真 really, 太 too / so, 最 most.
Exclamations: 太 + Adj + 了 ！ or 真 + Adj ！
patterns: 很 / 非常 / 真 / 最 + Adj
tips: 太 can also be negative ('too much'): 太 贵 了 means too expensive.

grammar.title: Comparing with 比
grammar.rule: A 比 B + Adjective. Negative: A 没有 B + Adjective.
body: No 很 in a 比 sentence. To state a difference, put it after the adjective: 大 两 岁.
'Not as … as' uses 没有: 我 没有 他 高.
tips: Wrong: 他 比 我 很 高.

ex.en: I'm not as tall as him.
My brother is two years older than me.

grammar.title: 和, 跟 and 一起
grammar.rule: A 和 / 跟 B: A and B, or with B. 一起 means together.
body: 和 joins nouns (我 和 他) and can mean 'with'. 跟 also means 'with' and 'follow'. 一起 stays before the verb.
你 跟 我 一起 去 = come with me.
tips: 和 joins nouns only. To join two verbs or sentences, just put them side by side.

ex.en: I go to the shop with my friend.
I learn Chinese from the teacher.
I have a brother and a sister.

grammar.title: 从 for 'from'
grammar.rule: 从 + place or time introduces where or when something starts.
body: 从 北京 来 comes from Beijing. 从 … 到 … gives a start and end: 从 家 到 学校.
tips: The 从 phrase goes before the verb.

ex.en: From home to school is far.

grammar.title: 吧 and 呢
grammar.rule: 吧 softens a suggestion or guess. 呢 follows up a question.
body: 吧 turns a statement into a suggestion (我们 走 吧) or a guess (你 是 学生 吧 ？).
呢 means 'and what about …?': 我 很 好 ， 你 呢 ？ With a place question it asks where: 你 的 书 呢 ？
tips: Don't pile them up with 吗; 吗 asks, 吧 suggests.

grammar.title: 请 and 别
grammar.rule: 请 + Verb is polite 'please'. 别 + Verb is 'don't'.
body: 请 坐, 请 进, 请 喝 茶. 别 forbids: 别 忘 了, 别 生气. The subject is dropped.
不用 means 'no need to': 不用 了.
tips: 别 is a command. For 'I don't want to' use 不 想.

grammar.title: 地 with adverbs
grammar.rule: Adj + 地 + Verb: 'doing it …-ly'.
body: 地 links a describing word to the verb it modifies, like English -ly. Many adjectives don't need it; it is common with two-syllable ones.
tips: 地 sounds the same as 的 (de). 的 follows modifiers of nouns, 地 follows modifiers of verbs.

grammar.title: Location words
grammar.rule: 上 下 里 外 前 后 左 右 东 南 西 北, plus 边 for the 'side'.
body: Add 边 to make the side: 上边 above, 下边 below, 里边 inside, 外边 outside, 前边 front, 后边 back, 左边 left, 右边 right, 旁边 beside, 中间 middle.
The place goes first, then the position: 桌子 上边, 学校 旁边. After a noun the short forms 上 and 里 are common: 桌子 上, 学校 里.
tips: 东 南 西 北 are east, south, west, north (Chinese lists east first).

ex.en: The bookstore is next to the school.
The shop is in front of the hospital.
My phone is on the table.
The library is on the left.
The shop is between the school and the hospital.

grammar.title: Money
grammar.rule: 块 (yuan, spoken), 毛 (10 cents), 分 (cent). 多少 钱 asks the price.
body: 三 块 五 is 3.50 yuan, one yuan five is 一 块 五 毛. In writing, 元 replaces 块.
How much: 这 个 多少 钱 ？ Answer: 十 块.
tips: The last unit can be dropped: 三 块 五 means three yuan fifty.

grammar.title: Some, a little
grammar.cn: 一些 / 有些 / 有的 / 一点儿
grammar.rule: 一些 some, 有的 some of them, 一点儿 a little.
body: 一点儿 goes with things you can't count: 一点儿 米饭. 一些 is a vague number. 有的 + noun picks out a part: 有的 人 …, 有的 人 …
tips: Say 一点儿 for 'a little', not 一些, when talking about mass nouns.

ex.en: I'd like a bit of rice.

grammar.title: Linking clauses
grammar.cn: 并列复句: 一边 … 一边 …
grammar.rule: 一边 … ， 一边 … = doing two things at once.
body: Two clauses can simply sit side by side with a comma. To show two actions at the same time use 一边 … 一边 …. To show 'too', put 也 in the second clause.
patterns: Subject + 一边 + Verb ， 一边 + Verb
tips: The subject appears once, at the front.

ex.en: He listens to songs while writing.
She is busy and I am busy too.

official.cn: 名词 / 方位名词 / 上、下、里、外、前、后、左、右、东、南、西、北；上边、下边、 里边、外边、前边、后边、左边、右边、东边、南边、西边、北边

动词 / 能愿动词 / 想、要

official.en: Degree adverbs (非常, 很, 太, 真, 最)
